2. Relevant facts for disposal of the Rule are that opposite party Nos. 1-28 as plaintiffs filed Other Suit No. 80 of 2004 before the court of Assistant Judge, Patiya, Chattogram against the petitioner and pro-forma opposite parties praying for determination of title of the plaintiffs to the disputed land and partition of the suit land, stating, inter alma, that the land in suit appertaining to RS Plot No. 905/ka465 corresponding to BS Plot Nos. 1714, 1816 and 1800 under RS khatian No. 1471 corresponding to RS khatian No. 1479 and BS khatian No. 1626 measuring an area of 15 decimal of land originally belonged to four brothers Ausiar Rahman, Tomiz Uddin, Altaf Ali and Abdul Barik and their names were correctly recorded in the RS khatian. As such Ausiar Rahman was owner of ¼ share in the disputed suit scheduled land. Plaintiff No. 13 Abdul Alim purchased 8 decimal of land from Kabir Ahmed, Laila Khatun, Modina Khatun, Bali Khatun, Md Kamal and Rasheda Begum heirs and subsequent heirs of RS recorded tenant Tomiz Uddin and from Habiza Khatun, Enamul Haque, Rizia Khatun, Hafez Mohammad Toiob, Nur Nahar Begum, Abul Monsur, Abul Mojur and Yeasmin Akter hens and subsequent heirs of RS recorded tenant Altaf Ali vide registered deed No. 1715 dated 16-5-2004. Other plaintiffs got 1 gonda 2 kora 1 kranti and 10 til land by way of inheritance. In the above way the plaintiffs are owner and possessor of 5 gonda 2 kora 1 kranti and 10 til land as stated in the 

 schedule to the plaint. But 13 decimal of land was wrongly recorded in RS and BS khatian in the name of the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-4 namely Mofizur Rahman and 2 decimal of land was wrongly recorded in the BS khatian in the name of the government. The plaintiffs on 6-8-2004 approached the defendants to make partition of the land but the defendants did not come forward, then the plaintiffs filed the suit for a decree of ascertaining their title and partition. 

 3. Defendant No. 1, the petitioner contested the suit by filing written statements contending, inter alia, that Ausiar Rahman, Tomiz Uddin, Abdul Barik and Altaf All were owner of 63 decimal of land appertaining to RS Plot Nos. 938/ 931 / ka484/ / ka4&3/ 925 // ka481 and 988/kki465 under RS khatian No. 1471. Abdul Batik mortgaged the land of disputed plot No. measuring an area of 15 decimal of land to Ahmed Ali by a registered mortgaged deed No. 331 dated 9-4-1931 and delivered possession to him. That transfer was cancelled due to the law of AK Fazlul Haque. Thereafter, Abdul Barik transferred the disputed land along with other land on receiving Taka 96 by a registered patta deed No. 963 dated 7-5-1941 to the said Ali Ahmed who continued the possession as before he got the possession on the basis of the mortgage deed. Ali Ahmed died leaving wife Mabia Khatun, and one daughter. Maleka Khatun. Maleka Khatun died leaving behind her husband Mofizur Rahman, mother Mabia Khatun including defendant Nos. 1-4 as her heirs. Mabia Khatun sold out her share to Mofizur Rahman. Mofizur Rahman in the above way and by means of amicable settlement got title and possession over the total land of the disputed plot measuring an area of 15 decimal and RS and RS record was prepared in his name correctly without any objection. After his death her son defendant No. 1 got the same by way of inheritance and since other heirs of Mofizur Rahman defendant Nos. 2-4 waived their title in favour of the defendant No. 1. Out of 15 decimal of land 2 decimal was acquired by the government for CUFL Road which was recorded in the name of the government in the BS khatian No. 1 in Plot No. 1800 and defendant No. 1 got the compensation (Award) for the said 2 decimal of land from the government. The plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the disputed land. The plaintiffs is an influential person who in collusion with the plaintiff created a false deed on 16-5-2004 long after the transfer made by RS recorded tenant Abdul Batik in favour of Ali Ahmed in the year 1931 and 1941 by registered deed Nos. 331 and 963 respectively and filed the test suit for a decree of determination of title and partition which is liable to be dismissed. 

 6. Mr HMA Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the learned Additional District Judge erred in law in rejecting the prayer for amendment of the written statement without considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the law related to the subject matter and, as such, occasioned failure of justice. He also submits that the proposed amendment of the written statement will not change the fundamental character of the defence rather it will facilitate the determination of real question in controversy between the parties. He adds that the defendant petitioner was unable to collect important relevant documents including some of those documents which more than seventy years old and necessary to arrive at correct decision in the suit. He again submits that 63 decimal of land appertaining to four RS Plots under RS khatian No. 1471 is the common ezmali property between the parties but the plaintiffs have filed the partition suit only for one RS plot No. 905/).465 measuring an area of 15 decimal of land wherein the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest as claimed by them. Thereafter, he adds that the defendant-petitioner by the proposed amendment brought into light the related eight registered deeds alongwith other important documents which are also necessary for taking correct decision in the suit. Furthermore he adds that the amendment petition should have been allowed by the learned Additional District Judge for complete and proper adjudication of the suit and to determine the real question in controversy between the parties to the suit. 

 9. I have heard the learned Advocate for both the sides and perused the materials on record meticulously. It appears from the amendment petition that the defendant No. 1 filed the amendment petition for stating in details how the defendant No. 1 Md Sekander Ali and the defendant No. 5 the government on behalf of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh  squired the total land of disputed RS Plot No. 905/ka465 measuring an area of 15 decimal and how rest of the other three RS recorded tenants Ausiar Rahman, Altaf Ali and Tamiz Uddin had transferred their land and possessed the rest of the property from the common and ezmali plot 938 / 931 / 925 / Nos. ka484, ka483/ ka481 under the disputed RS khatian No. 1471. For the above purpose the defendant No. 1 has mentioned in the amendment petition the deed Nos. 331, 963, 3058, 4120, 2220, 434, 1690, 1551, 4968, 4936, 3618 dated 9-4-1931, 7-5-1941, 8-7-1942, 28-10-1954, 28-10-1954, 10-2-1970, 15-5-1977, 30-4-1947, 9-12-1947, 29-10-1958 and 26-7-1958 respectively including LA Case No. 19/79-80, RS khatian No. 1471 and also submitted documents with a firisti which contained 8 registered deeds and 5 other documents relating to information slip dated 3-11-2021, RS khatian No. 16, BS khatian No. 680, 248 and BS khasra khatian No. 1110. As per claim of the defendant No. 1, those documents are necessary for determination of the rights real question in controversy between the parties. Moreover, on perusal of the record it appears that 63 decimal of land appertaining to RS plot / "92 5 / / Nos. 938 ka484/ 931/ka483f ka481 andA 905 ka465 under RS khatian No. 1471 was recorded correctly in the name of RS tenants Ausiar Rahman, Tamizuddin, Altaf Ali and Abdul Barik. So, the said 63 decimal of land is the common and ezmali property. But the plaintiffs have filed the suit praying for, inter alia, partition only for the RS Plot No. 9054a465 measuring an area of 15 decimal of land. As per claim of the defendant No. 1 Md Sekander Ali out of the said 15 decimal of land he has right, title and possession over 13 decimal of land and the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh has right, title and possession over rest of the 2 decimal of land, since this 2 decimal of land was acquired by the government for CUFL Road by the LA Case No. 19/1979-80.
